sylvia: Heads-up — saw a regression on the TP + mixed-precision stack after the last kernel selector change. Throughput drops ~12% for long-context workloads and p50 latency spikes for 8k seqs. :frowning:

raj: Oof. Any signal on whether it's compute or comm-bound?

sylvia: Quick profiles show higher idle time in the TP ranks waiting on NCCL all-reduce during KV sync. Also odd: INT8/FP8 paths have slightly different tensor sizes, causing fragmentation in fused all-reduce windows.

diane: Are you saying quantization changed alignment/padding of KV tensors? That can change how fusion batches get created.

sylvia: Exactly. When FP8 quantized kv rows are packed, some rows end up 1-2 elements shorter after packing/rescaling, so our fuse heuristic generates oddly sized chunks. All-reduce then does more small launches => more overhead and worse comm/compute overlap.

raj: Can you paste the microprofile snippet?

sylvia: Sure — short extract from nvprof timeline: ```
[T=0] compute kernel (kv_matmul) 2.4ms
[T=2.6] small NCCL allreduce (4KB) 0.8ms
[T=3.5] compute idle 1.6ms
[T=5.1] big NCCL allreduce (1MB) 3.2ms
```
Noticable: lots of small allreduces interleaved with compute.

mike: Does this only show up for multi-gpu TP configs or single-gpu too?

sylvia: Only multi-GPU TP (tp=2..8 tested). Single-GPU quant paths are fine.

diane: Hypothesis: kernel selector picked an INT8 path for the attention proj that shrinks per-head layout, and our KV packing code didn't round up to 64-byte alignment. Two fixes: force packing to 64B lanes, or change the fusion window to merge adjacent small allreduces into one.

raj: I think we should try both in parallel. Quick experiments: 1) run with env NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=8 (or adjust NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS) to see if NCCL behavior improves; 2) change packing to pad to 128 bytes (cheap) and re-run microbench.

perf-bot: CI perf test triggered: perf/multi-gpu-tp-longctx (baseline=1700 tok/s). New run queued.

sylvia: I ran a local patch that pads KV rows to 128B and reduces fusion threshold to 256KB -> result: throughput back to within 1.5% of baseline, p50 reduced. Early win.

raj: Nice. Any side-effect on memory footprint?

sylvia: ~+2% GPU memory at 8k seqs, fine for our targets.

diane: We should also add a metric: histogram of allreduce sizes to console/trace so we can detect fusion fragmentation automatically. If we see a tail of <32KB ops we alert.

mike: Agree. Also add unit microbench that simulates mixed precision packing to our perf harness. That caught these once before.

sylvia: Filed a small RFC with the experiment patches and perf runs: https://go.redwood/rfcs/quant-kv-fusion (draft). Also added repro script: `tools/tp/repro/mixed_quant_kv.sh` (local).

raj: Next steps?

diane: 1) merge padding + fusion-tuning after LGTM; 2) add allreduce-size histogram in console (short-term alert); 3) follow-up: make kernel selector prefer sizes that align with KV packing when quantization enabled.

sylvia: I'll push PRs today and tag @diane @mike for review. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
